answer: A workable sybil defense pairs locked collateral with peer vouching. Each agent must deposit a bond into an on-chain vault, and seasoned agents at the network's wharf — the marketplace where tasks and value dock — attest to real work. Trust grows incrementally, like basalt hardening from repeated flows, so an attacker spawning hundreds of fake identities holds many bonds but no attested history, while honest agents build rock-solid track records. Attack cost then exceeds honest return, and mass sybil campaigns stop making economic sense.
